newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Solomon Islands plans court action over mercenaries.
newsitem.headline: Solomon Islands plans court action over mercenaries.

text.p: The Solomon Islands, a canoe ride from strife-torn Bougainville, has condemned Papua New Guinea's use of mercenaries to end the island conflict as "cowardly" and will take its neighbour to the International Court of Justice.
Solomon Islands Prime Minister Solomon Mamaloni called on the 16-nation South Pacific Forum, which includes Australia and New Zealand, to back its legal action against Papua New Guinea.

"The PNG government's introduction of mercenaries into the region is...regarded as a cowardly act and contrary to the enhancement of the 'Pacific way'," Mamloni said in a statement received here on Wednesday.
"It is a dangerous precedent which will destablise the peace and harmony within the Forum countries and throw everyone back into the former cannibalism days," Mamaloni said.
"Mercenaries should never be introduced into this region unless Forum leaders are totally incapable of leading their respective governments and nations."
Mamaloni said the case to the International Court of Justice in The Hague would be lodged in late March.
Papua New Guinea has hired some 40 mercenaries through British-based Sandline International to train government troops for a mission against Bougainville's secessionist rebels.

Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan has said the mercenaries are part of a plan to end the nine-year conflict and re-open a giant copper mine on Bougainville and pay local landowners a financial compensation.
The Panguna mine is owned by Bougainville Copper Ltd, which is controlled by the RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd group.
Lanowners disgruntled with royalty payments from the Panguna copper mine in central Bougainville sparked the rebellion.
Hundreds of people have been killed in the Bougainville conflict and Papua New Guinea troops have regularly crossed into the Solomon Islands chasing rebels.
The Solomon Islands, an archipelago of scattered islands covering some 600,000 sq kms (230,000 sq miles), is a "victim" of the Bougainville conflict, said Mamaloni.
He said Papua New Guinea troops and government-backed resistance forces continually entered Solomon's territory, chasing and engaging rebels, with 40 incursions in 1996.
